newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam keeps currency nudging lower.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam keeps currency nudging lower.

text.p: Vietnam's central bank has pegged its official rate for the dong against the dollar slightly lower again, giving the local currency room to nudge down a few ticks in the interbank market, dealers said on Wednesday.
"The State Bank is keen to see the dong depreciate, but it's going at a glacial pace," said one dealer at a foreign bank in Ho Chi Minh City.
The central State Bank of Vietnam moved its official rate to 11,040 dong per dollar this week from 11,037.
Commercial banks may buy and sell at rates up to one percent either side of that rate, which means the new trading band has 10,930 as an upper dong limit and 11,150 as a lower dong limit.

With corporate demand for dollars strong, the dong has been moving directly to its lower limit each time the floor is lowered. Foreign banks were quoting rates of 11,140/11,150 per dollar and 11,137/48 on Wednesday.
However, dealers said the State Bank has been soaking up some of the demand for dollars and breathing some life into a moribund market by selling the U.S. currency at the lower dong limit.
One said the Bank had been selling up to $2 million a day in Ho Chi Minh City, where the black market rate for dong has dropped to around 11,270 per dollar.
The authorities are thought to be engineering a gradual depreciation of the local currency to help tackle a rapidly widening trade gap.

Official media reports said the trade deficit for the first 11 months of this year was $3.71 billion compared with $2.3 billion for the whole of 1995. Official confirmation of the figures was not immediately available.
One trader said he expected the State Bank to nudge the dong's lower limit down to 11,160 per dollar by the end of this month and then continue lowering it by about 20 dong per month after that.
Traders said that in addition to demand for dollars there was also illiquidity in the dong market, where money rates have firmed in recent weeks.
The State Bank will offer $50 billion ($4.49 billion) of six-month Treasury bills today, though traders said buying interest -- as in recent sales -- would be very low.
